Definition: from G1537 and G2212; to search out, i.e. (figuratively)investigate, crave, demand, (by Hebraism) worship:--en- (re-)quire, seek after (carefully, diligently).
BiblicalUsage: ekzētéō is how Scripture says to seek out, to require. In Luke 11:50, the text says "may be required of this generation." In Acts 15:17, the text says "That the residue of men might seek after the Lord."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, ekzētéō is a reminder that prayer is not a formula but a conversation — God hears, and He answers in His own time. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
